items.name: Mahamrityunjay Jaap
items.heroSubtitle: Arrange Mahamrityunjay Mantra Jaap performed by experienced priests on your behalf.
items.heroImageAlt: Sacred lamps and flowers arranged for a puja
items.jaapIntroText:
Mahamrityunjay Jaap is the sacred chanting of the Mahamrityunjay Mantra from the Rigveda, dedicated to Lord Shiva in his form as the conqueror of death. Performed in sets of 108, 1,008, or 1,25,000 repetitions, this jaap is believed to invoke Lord Shiva's grace for health, long life, protection, and liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

Our experienced priests perform the jaap on your behalf with a proper sankalp in your name and gotra, following Vedic procedures. You receive a recorded video and prasad.
items.jaapMeaning: We worship the three-eyed Lord Shiva, who is fragrant and nourishes all beings. May He free us from the bondage of death, just as a ripened cucumber is freed from its vine, and grant us liberation.
items.jaapCol1Text: The Mahamrityunjay Mantra addresses Lord Shiva as the three-eyed one who perceives past, present and future. Chanting it with devotion is believed to create a protective shield around the devotee.
items.jaapCol2Text: This jaap is performed for the recovery of serious illness, protection from untimely death, relief from grief and fear, and to seek Lord Shiva's blessings for a long and healthy life.
items.jaapCol3Text: The Mahamrityunjay Mantra appears in the Rigveda (7.59.12) and is one of the most powerful Vedic mantras. It is chanted in temples, hospitals, and homes to invoke divine protection and spiritual healing.

jaapFaqs.q: What is Mahamrityunjay Jaap?
jaapFaqs.a: Mahamrityunjay Jaap is the sacred repetition of the Mahamrityunjay Mantra from the Rigveda, dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is performed for health, protection, and to seek Lord Shiva's blessings.

jaapFaqs.q: How many times is the mantra chanted?
jaapFaqs.a: The jaap is offered in counts of 108, 1,008, 11,000 or 1,25,000 repetitions. The count is chosen based on your occasion and requirement.

items.name: Sundarkand Path
items.heroSubtitle: Arrange Sundarkand Path from the Ramcharitmanas, performed by experienced priests.
items.heroImageAlt: An open scripture with flowers beside it
items.jaapIntroText:
Sundarkand is the fifth chapter of the Ramcharitmanas composed by Goswami Tulsidas and also of the Valmiki Ramayana. It narrates the journey of Lord Hanuman to Lanka to find Mata Sita, and is considered the most sacred and powerful chapter of the Ramayana. Its recitation is believed to bring courage, peace, success, and relief from difficulties.

Our priests recite the complete Sundarkand Path on your behalf with a sankalp in your name, following traditional procedures.

items.jaapCol1Text: Sundarkand describes Lord Hanuman's flight to Lanka, his search for Mata Sita, his encounter with Ravana, and his return with news that brings hope to Lord Rama. It is the chapter of courage and devotion.
items.jaapCol2Text: The path is performed for the removal of obstacles, courage in difficult times, success in important endeavours, peace in the home, and to invoke Lord Hanuman's protection over the family.
items.jaapCol3Text: Sundarkand is considered so auspicious that its regular recitation is believed to ward off evil, remove fear, and bring the blessings of both Lord Rama and Lord Hanuman to the devotee's household.

items.name: Durga Saptashati Path
items.heroSubtitle: Arrange Durga Saptashati recitation performed by priests on your behalf with full tradition.
items.heroImageAlt: Lamps and offerings arranged for a Devi puja
items.jaapIntroText:
Durga Saptashati, also known as Devi Mahatmyam or Chandi Path, is a sacred text of 700 verses from the Markandeya Purana that describes the victory of Goddess Durga over the demon forces. It is one of the most important texts of Shakti worship and is recited during Navratri and other occasions dedicated to the Divine Mother.

Our priests recite the complete Durga Saptashati with a sankalp in your name, following traditional procedures with all thirteen chapters.
items.jaapMeaning: Salutations to the Goddess who resides in all beings in the form of Shakti (divine power). We bow to Her, again and again.
items.jaapCol1Text: The Durga Saptashati consists of 700 shlokas in 13 chapters describing three episodes of Goddess Durga's victory over demonic forces â€” Madhu-Kaitabh, Mahishasura, and Shumbha-Nishumbha.
items.jaapCol2Text: It is performed to seek Goddess Durga's blessings for protection, strength, removal of obstacles, success, and victory over adversity. It is especially recited for the well-being of the family during difficult times.
items.jaapCol3Text: The Durga Saptashati is one of the most sacred texts in the Shakta tradition. Its recitation during Navratri is considered especially powerful. Every verse is believed to carry the energy of the Divine Mother.

items.name: Hanuman Chalisa Path
items.heroSubtitle: Arrange Hanuman Chalisa recitation performed by experienced priests on your behalf.
items.heroImageAlt: Flowers and a diya arranged for a puja
items.jaapIntroText:
The Hanuman Chalisa is a devotional hymn of forty verses composed by Goswami Tulsidas in praise of Lord Hanuman. It is one of the most widely recited prayers in the Hindu tradition and is believed to invoke Lord Hanuman's protection, courage, and blessings. Its daily or special recitation is a part of millions of Hindu households.

Our priests recite the Hanuman Chalisa on your behalf in multiples of 108, 1,008, or more, with a sankalp in your name and full devotion.
items.jaapMeaning: Having cleansed the mirror of my mind with the dust of the Guru's lotus feet, I recite the pure glory of Shri Raghuvira, which bestows the four fruits of life.
items.jaapCol1Text: The Hanuman Chalisa is a forty-verse prayer composed by Tulsidas in the 16th century. It describes Lord Hanuman's divine qualities, his devotion to Lord Rama, and his role as a protector and remover of fear.
items.jaapCol2Text: It is recited for courage, protection from negative forces, relief from fear and anxiety, success in difficult tasks, and to seek Lord Hanuman's blessings for the family's well-being.
items.jaapCol3Text: The Hanuman Chalisa is believed to be especially powerful when recited on Tuesdays and Saturdays. Continuous recitation â€” 108 times or more â€” is considered an act of deep devotion to Lord Hanuman.

jaapFaqs.q: What is Rudrabhishek?
jaapFaqs.a: Rudrabhishek is the ritual bathing of the Shivalinga with panchamrit while reciting the Rudrashtadhyayi from the Yajurveda. It is one of the most powerful forms of Lord Shiva's worship.

jaapFaqs.q: What materials are used in the abhishek?

jaapFaqs.q: What is the difference between Laghu Rudra and Maharudra?
jaapFaqs.a: Laghu Rudra consists of eleven recitations of the Rudrashtadhyayi. Maharudra consists of one hundred and twenty-one recitations, performed over several days and considered the most complete form.

items.name: Vishnu Sahasranama Path
items.heroSubtitle: Arrange Vishnu Sahasranama recitation â€” the thousand names of Lord Vishnu â€” on your behalf.
items.heroImageAlt: An open scripture with a lotus and diya
items.jaapIntroText:
Vishnu Sahasranama is the sacred hymn of one thousand names of Lord Vishnu, found in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata. Bhishma Pitamah recited these names to Yudhishthira on the banks of the Ganga before his departure. It is one of the most important daily prayers in the Vaishnava tradition and is widely recited across all Hindu communities.

Our priests recite the complete Vishnu Sahasranama on your behalf with a sankalp in your name, following the traditional puja procedure.
items.jaapMeaning: Lord Vishnu is the universe itself, the controller of the past, present and future, the creator and sustainer of all beings, the soul within all creatures, and the cause of all existence.
items.jaapCol1Text: The Vishnu Sahasranama contains one thousand names of Lord Vishnu, each describing a divine attribute. The text is drawn from the Mahabharata and is recited daily by millions of devotees.
items.jaapCol2Text: It is recited for peace of mind, removal of obstacles, success in life, protection of the family, spiritual progress, and to seek Lord Vishnu's continuous blessings and grace.
items.jaapCol3Text: Reciting the Vishnu Sahasranama is believed to be equivalent to the merit of all other forms of worship. Bhishma declared it the supreme dharma and recommended its daily recitation for all who seek liberation.

items.jaapIntroText:
The Bhagavad Gita is the sacred conversation between Lord Krishna and Arjuna on the battlefield of Kurukshetra. It contains 700 shlokas across 18 chapters covering the path of duty, devotion, knowledge, and liberation. The Gita is considered the essence of all Vedic wisdom and is one of the most widely read scriptures in the world.

Our priests recite the complete Bhagavad Gita on your behalf with a sankalp in your name, following the traditional procedure with reverence and devotion.

items.jaapIntroText:
The Gayatri Mantra is the most sacred mantra of the Vedic tradition, appearing in the Rigveda (3.62.10). Known as the mother of the Vedas, it is addressed to Savitar â€” the divine sun â€” and invokes divine intelligence to illuminate the mind. The mantra is considered the essence of all Vedic wisdom and has been chanted by seekers for thousands of years.

Our Vedic priests perform the Gayatri Mantra Jaap on your behalf in complete sandhya puja procedure, with the sankalp in your name.

items.jaapCol1Text: The Gayatri Mantra is a 24-syllable Vedic mantra from the Rigveda, dedicated to the solar deity Savitar. It is traditionally recited at dawn, noon, and dusk in the Sandhya Vandanam ritual.
items.jaapCol2Text: Gayatri Mantra Jaap is performed for mental clarity, intelligence, academic success, spiritual progress, and to invite divine light into one's mind and life. It is especially recommended for students and seekers.
items.jaapCol3Text: The Gayatri Mantra is considered the most powerful of all Vedic mantras. Adi Shankaracharya and many sages have described its daily recitation as the highest duty of a Hindu devotee. It is the mantra of all mantras.

items.jaapIntroText:
Akhand Ramayana Path is the continuous, uninterrupted recitation of the complete Ramcharitmanas composed by Goswami Tulsidas. The word 'Akhand' means unbroken â€” the recitation continues without pause, day and night, until all seven Kandas (chapters) are complete, typically taking 24 hours. It is considered one of the highest acts of devotion to Lord Rama.

Our team of priests performs the Akhand Ramayana Path in shifts to maintain continuous recitation, with a sankalp in your name.
